snapshot.capital_scaled: ₹50 lakh–3 crore for your own line or large co-packer runs, cold chain and distribution
snapshot.margin_d2c: 50–60% gross margin selling online in multi-packs
snapshot.distribution_note: Getting into fridges and shelves is expensive; distributors want proven demand

tailwinds: Buyers are cutting sugar and looking for low-calorie, functional and natural drinks.
Quick-commerce apps have become a strong launch channel for new drinks in metros.
Co-packers now offer smaller runs for cans, PET bottles and tetra packs.
Indian flavours such as shikanji, kokum, jaljeera and regional teas have a loyal audience that global brands underserve.
headwinds: Coca-Cola, PepsiCo and Reliance's Campa compete hard on price and own most shop fridges.
Minimum order quantities for cans and bottles are high, so your first run ties up a lot of cash.
Freight is a large share of the cost because drinks are heavy and low value per kilo.
Sales depend heavily on summer; winter months can be very slow.
angle_2026: The big soft-drink companies have restarted a price war, so a cheaper cola or lemon drink will not survive. New beverage brands that work in 2026 either own a functional claim (no sugar, electrolytes, gut health), an Indian flavour with a story, or a premium occasion such as mixers and cafés.
cost_basis: Estimated for a brand using a co-packer, 2–3 SKUs and launching in one metro, 2026 prices.

setup_costs.covers: Food technologist, trial batches, stability testing
Minimum order of 10,000–30,000 units including cans or bottles
Label or can design, printing plates, cartons
Licence, nutrition and label claim testing
Storage, delivery to quick-commerce dark stores and distributors
Free samples at gyms, offices and events, creators, listing fees

unit_economics.note: Beverages make money only at volume. Selling online in packs of 6–24 improves margins, but freight on heavy parcels can wipe out the gain.

investor_probes: What is your cost per unit at 10,000 units, and at 1 lakh?
How many stores reorder without you visiting?
Why won't a big brand launch the same flavour at a lower price?
How much of your yearly sales comes in summer?
What do distributors and retailers take as margin?
bootstrap_takeaway: Start in one city with one hero flavour, sell in cafés, gyms and quick commerce first, and prove repeat orders before you pay for wide retail distribution.
sourcing_edge: Work with a co-packer that already makes a similar drink; they'll handle licensing, filling and quality checks. Buying cans or bottles jointly with other small brands can lower the minimum order.
licences: FSSAI state or central licence (manufacturing through a co-packer still needs your own licence as brand owner)
BIS certification for packaged drinking water or mineral water, if relevant
Legal Metrology labelling for packaged goods
Excise licence from the state for any alcoholic drink

hard_truths.title: Minimum orders lock up cash
hard_truths.text: A single run of cans can cost several lakh. If the flavour doesn't sell, you are left with stock that expires in 6–12 months.

hard_truths.title: Fridge space is controlled
hard_truths.text: The big brands give shops free fridges in exchange for keeping them stocked with their drinks. You'll mostly be on warm shelves unless you pay for placement.

hard_truths.title: Freight is brutal
hard_truths.text: A carton of drinks is heavy and cheap. Shipping it across the country can cost more than your margin, so build demand city by city.

hard_truths.title: Seasonality
hard_truths.text: Cold drinks sell most from March to June. Plan cash for slow winters, or add hot or all-season products.

plan_goal: The aim is 3,000 units sold, with at least 30 outlets or online buyers reordering on their own.

plan.title: Recipe and costing
steps: Develop 2–3 recipes with a food technologist.
Run blind taste tests with 50 people from your target audience.
Get quotes from 3 co-packers for minimum runs and cost per unit.

plan.title: First run
steps: Get your FSSAI licence and test the label claims in a lab.
Produce the smallest run you can for one hero flavour.
List on one or two quick-commerce apps in your city.

plan.title: Sample hard
steps: Give away samples at gyms, offices, colleges and events.
Pitch 20 cafés and restaurants and offer sale-or-return for the first month.
Collect feedback and reorder data every week.

plan.title: Review the numbers
steps: Calculate margin per unit after all freight and listing fees.
Keep the channels where buyers reorder.
Decide whether to add a flavour or a second city.
